S1.why: A bare noun phrase is how Korean labels a group; 개 is the counter the app already uses in “컷링 %lld개”.

S2.why: A -기 noun title invites without commanding and without picking a speech level; 마음껏 reads warm in all three states, even when nothing is saved yet.

S3.s: 무료 컷링 %lld개를 모두 채웠습니다. 저장한 컷링은 계속 무료로 쓸 수 있습니다.
S3.back: free cutling 5 [counter] all filled. saved cutlings-as-for continuing free-as use can.
S3.why: 채웠습니다 (filled) matches the five full tiles above; 계속 무료로 쓸 수 있습니다 says they stay free and keep working in one clause, in the app's 합니다체.

S4.why: 까지 carries the “up to” a Korean reader expects with a free allowance; 컷링 is the vocabulary file's word for an item.

S5.why: Korean says the whole before the part (5개 중 3개), so the placeholders are positional; same verb as S3.

S6.why: A noun-phrase row title, as Korean feature lists are written; ends on 까지 so the grey line below finishes the thought.

S7.why: 텍스트 and 이미지 are the app's own words, and 은/는 sets the two limits side by side; ends on 저장됩니다 so it does not repeat the 수 있습니다 of the subtitle above it.

S8.why: 및 is how Apple's Korean joins the last of three items; device names stay in Latin as Apple writes them.

S9.s: 한 번 구입하면 Apple 계정의 모든 기기에 적용됩니다.
S9.back: one time buy-if Apple account's all devices-to applies.
S9.why: Apple 계정 and 모든 기기 echo the app's existing iCloud sentence; 구입 is Apple Korea's word for an App Store purchase, used throughout.

S10.why: 만 (only) carries “nothing recurring” without naming the subscription twice; 결제 is the word Koreans use for paying at checkout.

S11.why: The repeated 도 is the native way to say “no this, no that, no the other”; 회원 가입 is the everyday term for creating an account.

S12.why: The wording Apple's own Korean apps use for Restore Purchases, kept with 구입 to match the App Store's term.

S13.why: Keeps S12's words so the link does not change shape while it works; 중 plus the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: 에 is the same after any price (원, $, ¥), unlike 로/으로 which would change with the price's last sound; 잠금 해제 is the iOS Korean verb for unlocking.

S15.why: S14 without its price, so the button keeps its words when the price arrives.

S16.why: The phrase Korean apps use on a dismiss that puts off rather than refuses.

S17.why: iOS Korean's own label for close buttons.

S18.why: A title in the person's own voice, as Korean copy often puts it (내 파일, 이제 내 차례): 이제 marks the moment, 전부 takes in the whole grid with the empty room, and 내 것 is ownership, with no count and no 합니다 ending to clash with 내.

S19.s: 구입해 주셔서 감사합니다. 컷링을 혼자 만드는 개발자에게 큰 힘이 됩니다.
S19.back: buying giving-honorific thank. cutling alone making developer-to big strength becomes.
S19.why: 큰 힘이 됩니다 is how Koreans say a purchase supports someone; 혼자 만드는 개발자 names the one maker plainly.

S20.s: 다시 오신 것을 환영합니다. 이전 구입을 복원했습니다.
S20.back: again came-honorific thing welcome. previous purchase restored.
S20.why: The standard Korean welcome-back in 합니다체, then the plain fact; 복원 matches the S12 link the person just tapped.

S21.why: A VoiceOver label reads best as a short noun phrase; positional placeholders because Korean puts the total first.

S22.why: Opens with the app's own count string, 컷링 %lld개, which needs no plural in Korean and so is right for 1, 2, 5 and 21; 이제 marks the new room.

S23.s: 잠금 해제되었습니다. 이제 컷링을 %@개까지 저장할 수 있습니다.
S23.back: unlock became. now cutling 5,000 [counter] up-to save can.
S23.why: Two short spoken sentences, the change first and the room second, in 합니다체.

S24.why: The purchase is the subject, so nobody is blamed; no period, as Korean alert titles go.

S25.s: 지금은 App Store에 연결할 수 없습니다. 잠시 후 다시 시도하십시오.
S25.back: now-as-for App Store-to connect cannot. moment after again try-please.
S25.why: 잠시 후 다시 시도하십시오 is Apple Korea's alert wording, and 하십시오 holds the 합니다체 level.

S26.s: App Store에서 이 구입이 확인되지 않았습니다.
S26.back: App Store-at this purchase-subject confirmed-not became.
S26.why: Said as what happened to the purchase, not as the App Store refusing, so it stays calm.

S27.s: 이 기기에 로그인된 Apple 계정에 컷링 구입 내역이 없습니다.
S27.back: this device-on signed-in Apple account-in cutling purchase history not-exist.
S27.why: 로그인된 Apple 계정 is the vocabulary file's phrase; 구입 내역 is the App Store's own word for purchase history.

S28.s: 무료 버전은 컷링 %lld개까지입니다. 앱을 한 번 잠금 해제하면 마음껏 저장할 수 있습니다.
S28.back: free version-as-for cutling 5 [counter] up-to-is. app once unlock-if to-heart's-content save can.
S28.why: 앱 names the app in the second sentence so 컷링 means only the items; 마음껏 repeats S2's word.

S29.why: A slash pair with the counter is how Korean UI writes a compact used-of-total; same order as the source numbers, so no positional forms.

K1.s: 무료 %lld개 모두 사용 · 탭하여 잠금 해제
K1.why: Clipped noun phrases fit one key's height; 탭하여 is iOS Korean's verb for tap, and the middle dot is a native separator.

M1.why: Korean Mac commands are object plus verbal noun, as in 설정 열기; 컷링 here is the app's name as the vocabulary file writes it.

M2.why: M1 with the ellipsis character because the button opens a window.

M3.why: A row label is a noun; its value M4 gives the count.

M4.why: The same compact pair as S29, so the free count looks the same on Mac and iPhone.

M5.why: The -됨 status ending Korean Settings uses for a state (켜짐, 연결됨).

M6.s: 한 번 구입하면 iPhone, iPad 및 Mac에서 모두 잠금 해제됩니다.
M6.back: one time buy-if iPhone, iPad and Mac-on all unlock-become.
M6.why: Opens like S9 so the promise is worded the same on every device; the section heading already names 컷링.

M7.s: 이 Apple 계정의 iPhone, iPad 및 Mac에서 잠금 해제되었습니다.
M7.back: this Apple account's iPhone, iPad and Mac-on unlocked-became.
M7.why: Past tense states it is done; Apple 계정 and the 및 list match S8 and S9.

M8.s: 컷링이 무료가 되기 전에 구입하셨으므로 잠금 해제가 그대로 유지됩니다. 일찍부터 함께해 주셔서 감사합니다.
M8.back: cutling-subject free-to become before bought-honorific-so unlock-subject as-is kept. early-from together-being giving-honorific thank.
M8.why: 함께해 주셔서 감사합니다 is how Korean services thank early supporters; the honorific -시- marks the person as the one who bought.
